text: The Legal System and the Legislative Process INTRODUCTION In order to understand legal terminology and the manner in which it is used, it is important to understand the legal system that it is used in and how new laws are created.
text_raw:
The Legal System and the Legislative Process 
INTRODUCTION 
In order to understand legal terminology and the manner in which it is used, it is important 
to understand the legal system that it is used in and how new laws are created.

text: It is impor- tant to know the log of laws, the different court systems, and how they interact with each d accordi how they are created—the source of the law.
text_raw:
It is impor- 
tant to know the log of laws, the different court systems, and how they interact with each 
d accordi how they are created—the source of the law.

text: Courts are elassified according to the type i cases that can be heard, what type of court it is, the authority a court has, and where the court is located in the judicial hierarchy.
text_raw:
Courts 
are elassified according to the type i cases that can be heard, what type of court it is, the 
authority a court has, and where the court is located in the judicial hierarchy.

text: A legislature is one source of law in the United States, so it is important to know how bills are introduced, where bills are introduced, and how they are considered and passed.
text_raw:
A legislature is one source of law in the United States, so it is important to know how 
bills are introduced, where bills are introduced, and how they are considered and passed.

text: In order to understand the law and the legal terms related to the law, it is helpful to understand the terms that describe the process by which law is written and the process of passing the law.

text: INTRODUCTION In the previous chapter, terms related to criminal law were discussed; in this chapter, terms related to criminal procedure are presented.
text_raw:
INTRODUCTION 
In the previous chapter, terms related to criminal law were discussed; in this chapter, terms 
related to criminal procedure are presented.

text: Many of the same terms associated with civil procedure also apply to criminal procedure.
text_raw:
Many of the same terms associated with civil 
procedure also apply to criminal procedure.

text: However, criminal procedure begins before the case is even filed; it extends into the investigation of the crime and the gathering of evi- dence, when a search warrant is needed and when police can search without a warrant.
text_raw:
However, criminal procedure begins before the 
case is even filed; it extends into the investigation of the crime and the gathering of evi- 
dence, when a search warrant is needed and when police can search without a warrant.

text: How someone is charged with a crime can vary; conviction and appeals are also part of criminal procedure.
text_raw:
How 
someone is charged with a crime can vary; conviction and appeals are also part of criminal 
procedure.

text: Several criminal procedure concepts originated from Supreme Court cases, such as the right to be free from unreasonable searches and seizures, the right to remain silent, and the right to a jury trial, so some terms discussed in Chapter 8, Constitutional Law, are also presented in this chapter.

Several criminal procedure concepts originated from Supreme Court cases, such 
as the right to be free from unreasonable searches and seizures, the right to remain silent, 
and the right to a jury trial, so some terms discussed in Chapter 8, Constitutional Law, are 
also presented in this chapter.

text: Constitution protects the rights of people accused of crimes.

text: WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS, BILL OF ATTAINDER, AND EX POST FACTO LAWS The first of the rights guaranteed by the Constitution is the writ of habeas corpus (rit of habe-ee-us kor-pus).
text_raw:
WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS, BILL OF ATTAINDER, 
AND EX POST FACTO LAWS 
The first of the rights guaranteed by the Constitution is the writ of habeas corpus (rit of 
habe-ee-us kor-pus).

text: The writ literally means “You have the body.” The writ of habeas cor- pus is a court order directing a governmental official having a person in custody to present the prisoner in court and explain to the court why the prisoner is in jail.
text_raw:
The writ literally means “You have the body.” The writ of habeas cor- 
pus is a court order directing a governmental official having a person in custody to present 
the prisoner in court and explain to the court why the prisoner is in jail.

text: If it is found a pris- oner is being held illegally, then the court can order the prisoner’s release.
text_raw:
If it is found a pris- 
oner is being held illegally, then the court can order the prisoner’s release.

text: This right is in- voked often after an initial appeal of a criminal conviction has been denied.
text_raw:
This right is in- 
voked often after an initial appeal of a criminal conviction has been denied.

text: The prisoner alleges that he or she is being held illegally, and requests that the writ be granted to force the state to prove that it is not holding the person illegally.
text_raw:
The prisoner 
alleges that he or she is being held illegally, and requests that the writ be granted to force 
the state to prove that it is not holding the person illegally.

text: The Constitution prohibits ex post facto laws, laws that make a particular act a crime that was not a crime at the time it was committed.
text_raw:
The Constitution prohibits ex post facto laws, laws that make a particular act a crime 
that was not a crime at the time it was committed.

text: An ex post facto law can also be a law that increases the punishment for a crime after it was committed, or lessens the bur- den of proof necessary to prove a crime.
text_raw:
An ex post facto law can also be a 
law that increases the punishment for a crime after it was committed, or lessens the bur- 
den of proof necessary to prove a crime.

text: For example, a person is serving a ten-year sentence for a violation of the federal Mann Act.

pened during a trial do not require the reversal of the decision by the appellate court, pro- 
vided these mistakes did not deny the defendant due process and did not affect the final 
outcome of the case.

text: In other words, the error was not prejudicial to the rights of the de- fendant.
text_raw:
In other words, the error was not prejudicial to the rights of the de- 
fendant.

text: Whenever an error is alleged as part of an appeal, the defendant is seeking either a reversal of the conviction and a dismissal of the case or reversal of the conviction and a new trial.

a reversal of the conviction and a dismissal of the case or reversal of the conviction and a 
new trial.

text: A new trial is a re-examination of the facts, or some part of the facts, by the same court after a verdict by the jury or a decision of the court.

A new trial is a re-examination of the facts, or some part of the facts, by the same 
court after a verdict by the jury or a decision of the court.

parties after the verdict has been reached.

text: OTHER POST-CONVICTION REMEDIES Even if a defendant’s appeal fails, there are other ways that a criminal conviction can be eliminated or removed from the records of a court.
text_raw:
OTHER POST-CONVICTION REMEDIES 
Even if a defendant’s appeal fails, there are other ways that a criminal conviction can be 
eliminated or removed from the records of a court.

text: Other post-conviction remedies are is- sued either by the executive or judiciary branch of government.
text_raw:
Other post-conviction remedies are is- 
sued either by the executive or judiciary branch of government.

text: COMMUTATION OF SENTENCE The first post-conviction remedy is a commutation of a criminal penalty.
text_raw:
COMMUTATION OF SENTENCE 
The first post-conviction remedy is a commutation of a criminal penalty.

text: Commutation (kom-yoo-tay-shun) is the lessening of a criminal penalty that makes the penalty less se- vere than the sentence that was originally imposed.
text_raw:
Commutation 
(kom-yoo-tay-shun) is the lessening of a criminal penalty that makes the penalty less se- 
vere than the sentence that was originally imposed.

text: For example, a prisoner on death row may have his sentence commuted or reduced to life imprisonment by the governor.
text_raw:
For example, a prisoner on death row 
may have his sentence commuted or reduced to life imprisonment by the governor.

text: PARDONS A pardon is an action by the executive branch of government (by the President of the United States or the governor of a state) that mitigates or sets aside the punishment imposed for a crime.
text_raw:
PARDONS 
A pardon is an action by the executive branch of government (by the President of the 
United States or the governor of a state) that mitigates or sets aside the punishment imposed 
for a crime.

text: The pardon not only sets aside the punishment, but also restores any civil rights that were taken away from the defendant because of the criminal conviction.
text_raw:
The pardon not only sets aside the punishment, but also restores any civil rights 
that were taken away from the defendant because of the criminal conviction.

text: Different types of pardons may be granted.
text_raw:
Different types 
of pardons may be granted.

text: The first is an absolute or full pardon.
text_raw: The first is an absolute or full pardon.

text: An absolute or full par- don frees the defendant and sets aside the conviction without any conditions being attached.
text_raw:
An absolute or full par- 
don frees the defendant and sets aside the conviction without any conditions being attached.

text: The conviction and the time served by the defendant are totally eliminated.
text_raw: The conviction and the time served by the defendant are totally eliminated.

text: A conditional pardon is granted when certain conditions have been met; the pardon is not effective until the conditions are met.
text_raw:
A conditional pardon is granted when certain conditions have been met; the pardon is 
not effective until the conditions are met.

text: The defendant must perform some act or some event must take place before the pardon becomes effective.
text_raw:
The defendant must perform some act or some 
event must take place before the pardon becomes effective.

text: For example, a defendant may have to admit to the crime committed and apologize to the victim before the pardon be- comes effective.
text_raw:
For example, a defendant may 
have to admit to the crime committed and apologize to the victim before the pardon be- 
comes effective.

text: A general pardon is given to every defendant who either participated in certain criminal activity or who violated a certain statute.
text_raw:
A general pardon is given to every defendant who either participated in 
certain criminal activity or who violated a certain statute.

text: For example, the President of the United States might grant a pardon to everyone who participated in a riot that began during a political rally.
text_raw:
For example, the President of 
the United States might grant a pardon to everyone who participated in a riot that began 
during a political rally.

text: If some activity is decriminalized (declared no longer illegal) by the passing of a statute, all defendants convicted of violating the old law can receive a gen- eral pardon.
text_raw:
If some activity is decriminalized (declared no longer illegal) by 
the passing of a statute, all defendants convicted of violating the old law can receive a gen- 
eral pardon.

text: CRIMINAL PROCEDURE | 59 EXPUNGEMENT OF RECORD Another post-conviction remedy is the expungement of record, the process whereby the record of a criminal conviction is either destroyed or sealed after a certain period of time.
text_raw:
CRIMINAL PROCEDURE | 59 
EXPUNGEMENT OF RECORD 
Another post-conviction remedy is the expungement of record, the process whereby the 
record of a criminal conviction is either destroyed or sealed after a certain period of time.

text: Juvenile records are often expunged after defendants reach the age of majority.
text_raw: Juvenile records are often expunged after defendants reach the age of majority.

text: One way records can be expunged is if a court of appeals reverses a conviction and then orders the expungement of the defendant’s criminal record.
text_raw:
One way 
records can be expunged is if a court of appeals reverses a conviction and then orders the 
expungement of the defendant’s criminal record.

text: Another way records can be expunged is if the conditions set by a court after conviction or set by statute have been complied with.
text_raw:
Another way records can be expunged is 
if the conditions set by a court after conviction or set by statute have been complied with.

text: CONCLUSION The entire purpose of criminal procedure is to make sure that every person’s constitutional rights are protected.
text_raw:
CONCLUSION 
The entire purpose of criminal procedure is to make sure that every person’s constitutional 
rights are protected.

text: These rights include the right to be free from unreasonable searches and seizures, the rights a person has if he or she is accused or arrested, the right to a fair and speedy trial, and the right to appeal.
text_raw:
These rights include the right to be free from unreasonable searches 
and seizures, the rights a person has if he or she is accused or arrested, the right to a fair and 
speedy trial, and the right to appeal.

text: The police can search without a warrant in several circumstances, e.g., when searching for concealed weapons, to preserve evidence of a crime, if the evidence is in plain view, or if it is subject to a lawful arrest.
text_raw:
The police can search without a warrant in several circumstances, e.g., when searching 
for concealed weapons, to preserve evidence of a crime, if the evidence is in plain view, or 
if it is subject to a lawful arrest.

text: However, if a search is illegal, then any information gath- ered is subject to the exclusionary rule and the fruit of the poisonous tree doctrine.
text_raw:
However, if a search is illegal, then any information gath- 
ered is subject to the exclusionary rule and the fruit of the poisonous tree doctrine.

text: When someone is arrested, he or she must be informed of his or her Miranda rights: the right to remain silent, to have an attorney present during questioning, to have an attorney appointed to represent him or her, and the right to halt all questioning.
text_raw:
When someone is arrested, he or she must be informed of his or her Miranda rights: the 
right to remain silent, to have an attorney present during questioning, to have an attorney 
appointed to represent him or her, and the right to halt all questioning.

text: Also, if arrested with- out a warrant, the person has the right to be brought before a magistrate.
text_raw:
Also, if arrested with- 
out a warrant, the person has the right to be brought before a magistrate.

text: 106 CHAPTER 6 ENFORCEMENT PROCESS ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS If an agency is responsible for enforcing rules and regulations, then because of due process of law requirements, there must be a procedure in place to determine if a rule or regulation was actually violated and what the penalty will be for the violation.

106 CHAPTER 6 
ENFORCEMENT PROCESS 
ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS 
If an agency is responsible for enforcing rules and regulations, then because of due process 
of law requirements, there must be a procedure in place to determine if a rule or regulation 
was actually violated and what the penalty will be for the violation.

text: If a violation of a rule or regulation is found, the agency may request an administrative hearing—a proceeding before the administrative agency consisting of arguments, a trial, or both to determine if a violation of the rules or regulations occurred and what sanctions should be imposed.
text_raw:

text: Pro- cedural rules in an administrative hearing are more relaxed than in a court hearing.
text_raw:

text: The hearing may take place before an administrative board, a body that has the au- thority to conduct a quasi-judicial hearing, a hearing officer, or an administrative law judge (ALJ).

text: APPEALS BASIS FOR AN APPEAL If the defendant in the administrative proceeding is not satisfied with a decision, he or she has the right to appeal the decision to a court of law for judicial review.

APPEALS 
BASIS FOR AN APPEAL 
If the defendant in the administrative proceeding is not satisfied with a decision, he or she 
has the right to appeal the decision to a court of law for judicial review.

text: Judicial review is the power of the court to review decisions of another department or level of government.
text_raw:

is the power of the court to review decisions of another department or level of government.

text: In order for the court to hear the appeal, the person bringing the appeal must state a rea- son for the appeal—explain why the decision of the administrative agency is in error and should be reversed.

son for the appeal—explain why the decision of the administrative agency is in error and

text: This doctrine states that relief must be sought through all of the appropriate agency channels before a person can request a court to hear the case and grant relief.
text_raw:

text: STANDARD ON APPEAL When the case is appealed to a court, the court will apply a standard of review that will be used to determine whether or not to uphold the agency decision or reverse it.

STANDARD ON APPEAL 
When the case is appealed to a court, the court will apply a standard of review that will be

text: The standard that will be used by the court is the substantial evidence rule—evidence that a reasonable mind might accept as adequate to support a conclusion.
text_raw:

that will be used by the court is the substantial evidence rule—evidence that a reasonable 
mind might accept as adequate to support a conclusion.

text: Put another way, this is evidence that a reasonable person would accept as being enough to support a decision made by the agency.

Put another way, this is evidence

text: i CHAPTER 9 ga Torts INTRODUCTION Just as criminal law provides for “remedies” that are available to the state to punish peo- ple who violate other people’s rights by breaking the law, tort law provides for civil remedies for people who have had their rights violated by the actions of others.
text_raw:
i CHAPTER 9 ga 
Torts 
INTRODUCTION 
Just as criminal law provides for “remedies” that are available to the state to punish peo- 
ple who violate other people’s rights by breaking the law, tort law provides for civil 
remedies for people who have had their rights violated by the actions of others.

text: In fact, some torts can also be crimes.
text_raw:
In fact, 
some torts can also be crimes.

text: Tort law provides a method of compensation for a private person who has been injured by the intentional or negligent acts of another person or persons.
text_raw:
Tort law provides a method of compensation for a private 
person who has been injured by the intentional or negligent acts of another person or 
persons.

text: This chapter defines what a tort is and describes intentional torts and torts based upon negligence.

This chapter defines what a tort is and describes intentional torts and torts based upon 
negligence.

text: Who can commit a tort as well as who can be held liable and why are discussed.
text_raw: Who can commit a tort as well as who can be held liable and why are discussed.

text: The types of damages that can be received for the harm caused and the defenses that can be raised to tort claims are also presented.

The types of damages that can be received for the harm caused and the defenses that can be 
raised to tort claims are also presented.

text: GENERAL PRINCIPLES A tort is a private or civil wrong or injury, other than an action for a breach of contract, for which the court will provide a remedy in the form of a cause of action for the damages suf- fered.
text_raw:
GENERAL PRINCIPLES 
A tort is a private or civil wrong or injury, other than an action for a breach of contract, for 
which the court will provide a remedy in the form of a cause of action for the damages suf- 
fered.

text: A tort is a violation of a duty imposed by law for which a person may sue another person, in court, for damages.
text_raw:
A tort is a violation of a duty imposed by law for which a person may sue another 
person, in court, for damages.

text: In order to sue someone using tort law, there must be harm caused or about to be caused, and there must be the possibility of being compensated by a lawsuit seeking payment of damages.
text_raw:
In order to sue someone using tort law, there must be harm 
caused or about to be caused, and there must be the possibility of being compensated by a 
lawsuit seeking payment of damages.

text: LIABILITY AND TORTFEASORS If someone commits a tort, he or she can be held liable for his or her conduct.
text_raw:
LIABILITY AND TORTFEASORS 
If someone commits a tort, he or she can be held liable for his or her conduct.

text: Being held liable means being bound or obliged in law or equity to provide compensation to another for harm caused by one’s actions or by one’s failure to act.
text_raw:
Being held 
liable means being bound or obliged in law or equity to provide compensation to another 
for harm caused by one’s actions or by one’s failure to act.

text: Liability (lye-9-bil-i-tee) is a legal obligation to do, pay, or make good something, and this obligation may be enforced by a court of law.

Liability (lye-9-bil-i-tee) is a 
legal obligation to do, pay, or make good something, and this obligation may be enforced 
by a court of law.

text: Conduct, either by commission or omission, that may subject a person or business to li- ability under the principles of the law of torts is described as tortious.
text_raw:
Conduct, either by commission or omission, that may subject a person or business to li- 
ability under the principles of the law of torts is described as tortious.

text: Tortious conduct can lead to a person’s being forced to pay someone else for the harm caused by his or her ac- tion or inaction.

Tortious conduct can 
lead to a person’s being forced to pay someone else for the harm caused by his or her ac- 
tion or inaction.

text: The tortfeasor (tort-fee-zer) is the person or business that commits the tort.

text: A listing is the agreement between the owner of the real property and the real estate agent regarding the sale of the real estate.

A listing is the agreement between 
the owner of the real property and the real estate agent regarding the sale of the real estate.

text: Under the terms of the listing, the agent agrees to attempt to locate a buyer for the property at a certain price and at certain terms for a fee or commission.

Under the terms of the listing, the agent agrees to attempt to locate a buyer for the property 
at a certain price and at certain terms for a fee or commission.

text: Listings are classified in a number of ways.

text: An open listing is one that may be given to more than one agent at a time.
text_raw:
An open listing is one that may be given to 
more than one agent at a time.

text: The seller of the real estate is obliged to pay the commission of the real estate agent who locates a buyer if that agent is one of the authorized agents.

The seller of the real estate is obliged to pay the commission 
of the real estate agent who locates a buyer if that agent is one of the authorized agents.

text: The real estate agent who actually locates the buyer of the property is the person who collects the fee, even if he or she was not the real estate agent with whom the property was origi- nally listed.

The 
real estate agent who actually locates the buyer of the property is the person who collects 
the fee, even if he or she was not the real estate agent with whom the property was origi- 
nally listed.

text: If the owner of the property finds the buyer, however, he or she is under no ob- ligation to pay a commission to the real estate agent.
text_raw:

216 CHAPTER 12

Mortgages are classified based on who issues them, payment type, and interest rate.

text: A con- ventional mortgage is a contract that uses all or part of the property to secure the loan that is used to purchase the property; the borrower retains possession of the property.
text_raw:
A con- 
ventional mortgage is a contract that uses all or part of the property to secure the loan

text: A FHA mortgage is insured by the Federal Housing Administration in whole or in part.

text: The rate may or may not have a maximum limit.

or may not have a maximum limit.

cannot go up more than a certain percentage each year.

text_raw:

an ARM mortgage; the terms of the mortgage state that the maximum interest rate that can 
be charged 1s 12% and that the interest rate can increase by a maximum of 1% a year.

text: Thus, the most the interest rate can go up in a year is 1%; the highest the rate can go is 12%, re- gardless of what the rate index is.
text_raw:
Thus, 
the most the interest rate can go up in a year is 1%; the highest the rate can go is 12%, re- 
gardless of what the rate index is.

text: A balloon payment mortgage is one that requires interest payments for a specified pe- riod and full payment of the principal at the end of that period.
text_raw:
A balloon payment mortgage is one that requires interest payments for a specified pe- 
riod and full payment of the principal at the end of that period.

text: When a buyer makes an offer on real estate, there may be a clause in the offer similar to the following statement: “This offer is subject to the buyer’s being able to obtain suitable financing.” This statement is known as a mortgage contingency clause; the purchase of the real property is contingent on the buyer’s being able to acquire a mortgage or “suitable financing.” The mortgage contingency clause is designed to protect the buyer of the prop- erty in the event he or she is unable to obtain a loan to purchase the property.
text_raw:
When a buyer makes an offer on real estate, there may be a clause in the offer similar to 
the following statement: “This offer is subject to the buyer’s being able to obtain suitable 
financing.” This statement is known as a mortgage contingency clause; the purchase of 
the real property is contingent on the buyer’s being able to acquire a mortgage or “suitable 
financing.” The mortgage contingency clause is designed to protect the buyer of the prop- 
erty in the event he or she is unable to obtain a loan to purchase the property.

text: Securities INTRODUCTION Securities law relates to the types of securities that are traded or sold and the people who trade or sell them.
text_raw:
Securities 
INTRODUCTION 
Securities law relates to the types of securities that are traded or sold and the people who 
trade or sell them.

text: This chapter introduces and explains the terms used to describe the peo- ple who sell and buy securities, how they are bought and sold, the types of securities avail- able, and the regulations concerning their sale.

Arkansas Code Annotated § 23-42-405 
FEDERAL LAW REGULATING SECURITIES—SECURITIES ACTS 
Securities acts are federal and state statutes that govern the registration, the offering for 
sale, and the actual sale of securities.

text: There are two major federal securities acts: the Secu- rities Act of 1933 and the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.

found at 15 U.S.C. § 77a, regulates the registration of securities that are offered for sale to 
the public.

text: The Act mandates the disclosure of complete information regarding the issue of stock and the stock offering.

stock and the stock offering.

text: It also mandates the full disclosure of all material information about a security, the people who are issuing the security, and the intended use of the money that is being raised from the sale.

about a security, the people who are issuing the security, and the intended use of the money 
that is being raised from the sale.

text: The term material information is understood as all rel- - evant information that an investor would want to know about a company, its background, its executives, and its plan of operation.

evant information that an investor would want to know about a company, its background, 
its executives, and its plan of operation.

of the stock exchanges and over-the-counter markets.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: HOSTILE TAKEOVERS Because stocks of so many companies are publicly sold, and because stock ownership rep- resents ownership of a company, one company may attempt to take over another company by purchasing the other company’s stock.
text_raw:
HOSTILE TAKEOVERS 
Because stocks of so many companies are publicly sold, and because stock ownership rep- 
resents ownership of a company, one company may attempt to take over another company 
by purchasing the other company’s stock.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: There are several different terms and phrases that apply to situations when this happens.
text_raw:
There are several different terms and phrases that 
apply to situations when this happens.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: RAIDERS AND TAKEOVER BIDS A raider is a person or company that attempts to take control of a target company by buy- ing a controlling interest in its stock and installing new management.
text_raw:
RAIDERS AND TAKEOVER BIDS 
A raider is a person or company that attempts to take control of a target company by buy- 
ing a controlling interest in its stock and installing new management.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: If a raider accumu- lates more than 5% of the company stock, he or she must publicly report the purchase according to the Williams Act, 15 U.S.C. § 78.
text_raw:
If a raider accumu- 
lates more than 5% of the company stock, he or she must publicly report the purchase 
according to the Williams Act, 15 U.S.C. § 78.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: A takeover bid is an attempt by an outside corporation or group—usually termed the aggressor or insurgent—to take control of a company away from current management.
text_raw:
A takeover bid is an attempt by an outside corporation or group—usually termed the 
aggressor or insurgent—to take control of a company away from current management.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: A takeover bid may involve the purchase of shares of stock, a tender offer, a sale of assets, or a proposal that the company merge voluntarily with the aggressor.
text_raw:
A 
takeover bid may involve the purchase of shares of stock, a tender offer, a sale of assets, or 
a proposal that the company merge voluntarily with the aggressor.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: A target company is the object of an attempt at takeover by way of a tender offer or leveraged buyout.

A target company is the 
object of an attempt at takeover by way of a tender offer or leveraged buyout.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: LEVERAGED BUYOUT AND TENDER OFFERS A leveraged buyout is a method used to purchase outstanding shares of publicly traded stock by management or by outsiders.
text_raw:
LEVERAGED BUYOUT AND TENDER OFFERS 
A leveraged buyout is a method used to purchase outstanding shares of publicly traded 
stock by management or by outsiders.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be

text_raw:
The financing to purchase the stock comes primarily 
from funds borrowed from investment bankers or brokers.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: The money used for the buyout is usually secured by the target company’s assets, with the money to repay the funds bor- rowed coming from the company’s earnings or sales of some of its assets.
text_raw:
The money used for the buyout 
is usually secured by the target company’s assets, with the money to repay the funds bor- 
rowed coming from the company’s earnings or sales of some of its assets.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: Essentially what happens is a company borrows money to purchase enough stock of another company in or- der to take over and then dismantles all or part of the acquired company to pay back the loans.

happens is a company borrows money to purchase enough stock of another company in or-

text: DEFENSES TO TAKEOVER ATTEMPTS The target company may attempt several strategies to prevent the hostile takeover.

DEFENSES TO TAKEOVER ATTEMPTS 
The target company may attempt several strategies to prevent the hostile takeover.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be

text_raw:
Some 
can be done prior to a takeover bid; others take place after the attempt has begun.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: Two mea- sures that can be taken prior to a takeover attempt are lock ups and porcupine provisions.

Two mea- 
sures that can be taken prior to a takeover attempt are lock ups and porcupine provisions.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: Lock up is a slang term referring to the company’s setting aside securities to be purchased by a friendly interest in order to defeat or make more difficult any takeover attempt.
text_raw:
Lock up is a slang term referring to the company’s setting aside securities to be purchased 
by a friendly interest in order to defeat or make more difficult any takeover attempt.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: A por- cupine provision in either the company’s by-laws or its articles of incorporation is de- signed to make takeover attempts either impossible or impractical if the potential acquirer does not have the consent of the management of the company.
text_raw:
A por- 
cupine provision in either the company’s by-laws or its articles of incorporation is de- 
signed to make takeover attempts either impossible or impractical if the potential acquirer 
does not have the consent of the management of the company.

text: A target company may also attempt greenmail or a poison pill.
text_raw: A target company may also attempt greenmail or a poison pill.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: Greenmail is the pay- ment made by a target company to buy back shares of stock held by a potential acquirer of a company at a premium over the market value.
text_raw:
Greenmail is the pay- 
ment made by a target company to buy back shares of stock held by a potential acquirer of 
a company at a premium over the market value.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: In return, the person or institution agrees not to continue with the hostile takeover.
text_raw:
In return, the person or institution agrees 
not to continue with the hostile takeover.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: A poison pill is a defensive tactic used by a com- pany to prevent a hostile takeover.
text_raw:
A poison pill is a defensive tactic used by a com- 
pany to prevent a hostile takeover.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: The company makes its shares of stock or its financial condition less attractive to the potential acquirer.
text_raw:
The company makes its shares of stock or its financial 
condition less attractive to the potential acquirer.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: One method of doing so is to issue a new series of preferred stock that compels redemption at premium prices if there is a hostile takeover of the company.
text_raw:
One method of doing so is to issue a new 
series of preferred stock that compels redemption at premium prices if there is a hostile 
takeover of the company.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: Another method is to burden the company with high debt that will have to be paid by the person or institution attempting to acquire the company if the takeover bid is successful.
text_raw:
Another method is to burden the company with high debt that will 
have to be paid by the person or institution attempting to acquire the company if the 
takeover bid is successful.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: The target company may also seek for a white knight: a poten- tial acquirer who will rescue it from the unwanted takeover attempt.
text_raw:
The target company may also seek for a white knight: a poten- 
tial acquirer who will rescue it from the unwanted takeover attempt.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: One thing a raider may attempt to do in an effort to take over a company is to provide golden parachutes to key figures in the corporation.

One thing a raider may attempt to do in an effort to take over a company is to provide golden 
parachutes to key figures in the corporation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 15 REVIEW He Pua ae Be
text: The term golden parachute refers to a termina- tion agreement that shelters executives from the effects of a corporate change such as a hostile takeover.

INTRODUCTION 
Antitrust is an area of federal statutory law designed to protect consumers from monopo- 
lies, which occur when one company so dominates a market that consumers have only one

ANTITRUST ANALYSIS 
In order to determine if a business arrangement or a business practice is, in fact, illegal, an

text: No one method or test is used to make that determination.

No one method or test is

text: THEORIES Antitrust laws are designed to guard against unlawful restraints on commerce, price fix- ing, and the creation of monopolies.

THEORIES 
Antitrust laws are designed to guard against unlawful restraints on commerce, price fix- 
ing, and the creation of monopolies.

The primary purpose of antitrust law—the reason it

text: In order to determine if a trust situation exists, two general theories of antitrust analysis—the Chicago school and the Harvard school—are involved.

In 
order to determine if a trust situation exists, two general theories of antitrust analysis—the 
Chicago school and the Harvard school—are involved.

text: The Chicago school is based solely on the goal of economic efficiency or the maximization of consumer welfare.

The Chicago school is based solely 
on the goal of economic efficiency or the maximization of consumer welfare.

text: The Harvard school is an approach to antitrust policy based on the desirability of preserving competition to prevent the accumulation of economic and political power, the dislocation of labor, and market inefficiency.

text: The courts have looked at business activity in two ways to determine if antitrust laws have been violated.

if antitrust laws have been violated.

text: The first method used by the courts is the per se rule.
text_raw: The first method used by the courts is the per se rule.

text: This method states that certain business agreements, arrangements, or activity will auto- matically be held to be illegal by the courts because the courts assume that the arrangement will almost always result in a substantial restraint of trade.

matically be held to be illegal by the courts because the courts assume that the arrangement

text: The second method used is the rule of reason, which declares that only an unreasonable restraint of trade violates the Sherman Antitrust Act.

The second method used is the rule of reason, which declares that only an unreasonable 
restraint of trade violates the Sherman Antitrust Act.

text: Using the rule of reason, the court 1s required to weigh all the circumstances of the case, the history of the restraint, the evil that is believed to exist, the reason for adopting the particular remedy, and the result that is sought.

text: INTRODUCTION The area of labor law relates generally to unions and their dealings with employers and em- ployees.

INTRODUCTION 
The area of labor law relates generally to unions and their dealings with employers and em- 
ployees.

text: Labor law did not exist at common law; it was created by federal and state statute.
text_raw: Labor law did not exist at common law; it was created by federal and state statute.

management, and regulated internal union affairs.

THE WAGNER ACT (NATIONAL LABOR RELATIONS ACT) 
The next federal statute, the Wagner Act of 1935, also known as the National Labor Re- 
lations Act, provided employees with the right to organize, form, and join unions; bargain 
collectively through the unions; and engage in concerted activities to support their bar- 
gaining positions.

chapter_title: PART II. EMPLOYEES’ RIGHTS AND EMPLOYERS’ RESPONSIBILITIES

chapter_title: PART II. EMPLOYEES’ RIGHTS AND EMPLOYERS’ RESPONSIBILITIES
text: WORKERS’ COMPENSATION When an employee is injured on the job, workers’ compensation is usually the remedy available for that employee.
text_raw:
WORKERS’ COMPENSATION 
When an employee is injured on the job, workers’ compensation is usually the remedy 
available for that employee.

chapter_title: PART II. EMPLOYEES’ RIGHTS AND EMPLOYERS’ RESPONSIBILITIES
text: Workers’ compensation is set by state statute and provides for fixed awards to workers who are victims of employment-related accidents or injuries and their dependents.
text_raw:
Workers’ compensation is set by state statute and provides 
for fixed awards to workers who are victims of employment-related accidents or injuries 
and their dependents.

chapter_title: PART II. EMPLOYEES’ RIGHTS AND EMPLOYERS’ RESPONSIBILITIES
text: STRICT LIABILITY AND WORKERS’ COMPENSATION INSURANCE The effect of workers’ compensation is to make the employer strictly liable for injury sus- tained by an employee during the scope of and arising out of the course of employment.
text_raw:
STRICT LIABILITY AND WORKERS’ COMPENSATION INSURANCE 
The effect of workers’ compensation is to make the employer strictly liable for injury sus- 
tained by an employee during the scope of and arising out of the course of employment.

chapter_title: PART II. EMPLOYEES’ RIGHTS AND EMPLOYERS’ RESPONSIBILITIES
text: If an employee is injured on the job and the injury occurred as a result of work being per- formed, the employer is liable for that injury.
text_raw:
If 
an employee is injured on the job and the injury occurred as a result of work being per- 
formed, the employer is liable for that injury.

chapter_title: PART II. EMPLOYEES’ RIGHTS AND EMPLOYERS’ RESPONSIBILITIES
text: This liability is not unlimited; there are statu- tory limits on how much the injured worker can receive.
text_raw:
This liability is not unlimited; there are statu- 
tory limits on how much the injured worker can receive.

chapter_title: PART II. EMPLOYEES’ RIGHTS AND EMPLOYERS’ RESPONSIBILITIES
text: Workers’ compensation is usually an exclusive remedy:

an exclusive remedy:

sue the employer in tort law.

chapter_title: PART II. EMPLOYEES’ RIGHTS AND EMPLOYERS’ RESPONSIBILITIES

text: Workers’ compensation did not exist at common law; it was created by state statute.

chapter_title: PART II. EMPLOYEES’ RIGHTS AND EMPLOYERS’ RESPONSIBILITIES
text: Every state has its own workers’ compensation law governing employers in that particular state with each law having its own set of definitions.
text_raw:
Every state has its own workers’ compensation law governing employers in that particular 
state with each law having its own set of definitions.

chapter_title: PART II. EMPLOYEES’ RIGHTS AND EMPLOYERS’ RESPONSIBILITIES
text: There is no overarching federal law governing workers’ compensation that applies to all the states; every state’s laws are dif- ferent.

governing workers’ compensation that applies to all the states; every state’s laws are dif-

text: Intellectual Property INTRODUCTION The law of property deals with three types of property: real property, personal property, and intellectual property.
text_raw:
Intellectual Property 
INTRODUCTION 
The law of property deals with three types of property: real property, personal property, 
and intellectual property.

text: The law of real and personal property is based primarily on common law, although some areas of the law are based on statutes.
text_raw:
The law of real and personal property is based primarily on 
common law, although some areas of the law are based on statutes.

text: The law of intellec- tual property is based primarily upon statutory law, with some principles finding their basis in common law.
text_raw:
The law of intellec- 
tual property is based primarily upon statutory law, with some principles finding their 
basis in common law.

text: Some of the principles of common law have been incorporated into the statutes.
text_raw:
Some of the principles of common law have been incorporated 
into the statutes.

text: Intellectual property is the physical or tangible result of original thought, the physical manifestation of a person’s thoughts or ideas.
text_raw:
Intellectual property is the physical or tangible result of original thought, the physical 
manifestation of a person’s thoughts or ideas.

text: Four types of intellectual property will be dis- cussed in this chapter: copyrights, trademarks, patents, and trade secrets.
text_raw:
Four types of intellectual property will be dis- 
cussed in this chapter: copyrights, trademarks, patents, and trade secrets.

text: COPYRIGHT GENERAL PRINCIPLES Copyright applies primarily to written works.
text_raw:
COPYRIGHT 
GENERAL PRINCIPLES 
Copyright applies primarily to written works.

text: Anything that can be put in writing—books, magazine articles, music, movie scripts, a movie itself, even photographs—may be pro- tected by copyright.
text_raw:
Anything that can be put in writing—books, 
magazine articles, music, movie scripts, a movie itself, even photographs—may be pro- 
tected by copyright.

text: Copyright, which is governed by the federal 1976 Copyright Act, is an intangible right granted by statute to the author or originator of original works that are created.

trademark by the Patent and Trademark Office.

text: TYPES OF TRADEMARKS There are several different types of trademarks, and whether or not one can be registered depends on the type of mark it is.

TYPES OF TRADEMARKS 
There are several different types of trademarks, and whether or not one can be registered 
depends on the type of mark it is.

text: A descriptive trademark directly conveys to the buyer the ingredients, qualities, or characteristics of the product; in short, it describes the product to the consumer.

A descriptive trademark directly conveys to the buyer 
the ingredients, qualities, or characteristics of the product; in short, it describes the product 
to the consumer.

text: A suggestive trademark, on the other hand, is one that requires the buyer to use thought, imagination, or perception to connect the goods with the mark.

A suggestive trademark, on the other hand, is one that requires the buyer 
to use thought, imagination, or perception to connect the goods with the mark.

text: This type of trademark suggests what the product is to the consumer, but the consumer must use his or her imagination to determine what the product is.

This type of 
trademark suggests what the product is to the consumer, but the consumer must use his or 
her imagination to determine what the product is.

text: A fanciful trademark is a made-up or coined term or word.

text: ELECTRONIC FUNDS TRANSFER ACT The Electronic Funds Transfer Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1693, governs the rights and liabilities of consumers, financial institutions, and retailers who use electronic funds transfer systems.
text_raw:
ELECTRONIC FUNDS TRANSFER ACT 
The Electronic Funds Transfer Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1693, governs the rights and liabilities 
of consumers, financial institutions, and retailers who use electronic funds transfer systems.

text: An electronic funds transfer is a transaction that involves a financial institution and that is performed using a computer, a telephone, or other electronic instrument.
text_raw:
An electronic funds transfer is a transaction that involves a financial institution and that 
is performed using a computer, a telephone, or other electronic instrument.

text: The electronic funds transfer is usually initiated by a bank customer, the originator, who requests the bank to transfer credit to the account of another person, the beneficiary, who usually has an ac- count in a another bank.
text_raw:
The electronic 
funds transfer is usually initiated by a bank customer, the originator, who requests the bank 
to transfer credit to the account of another person, the beneficiary, who usually has an ac- 
count in a another bank.

text: One of the protections of the Act is the amount of liability a con- sumer faces if there are unauthorized transactions.
text_raw:
One of the protections of the Act is the amount of liability a con- 
sumer faces if there are unauthorized transactions.

text: Regulation E, promulgated by the Federal Reserve Board, sets out the consumer’s lia- bility.
text_raw:
Regulation E, promulgated by the Federal Reserve Board, sets out the consumer’s lia- 
bility.

text: Regulation E states that if the bank is notified within two days of the consumer’s learning about the unauthorized transaction, the consumer’s liability is limited to $50.
text_raw:
Regulation E states that if the bank is notified within two days of the consumer’s 
learning about the unauthorized transaction, the consumer’s liability is limited to $50.

text: If the bank is notified more than two days after the unauthorized transaction but within 60 days, the amount of liability is limited to $500.
text_raw:
If the 
bank is notified more than two days after the unauthorized transaction but within 60 days, 
the amount of liability is limited to $500.

text: If more than 60 days have passed since the unau- thorized transaction, the consumer faces unlimited liability.
text_raw:
If more than 60 days have passed since the unau- 
thorized transaction, the consumer faces unlimited liability.

text: CONSUMER LEASING ACT The Consumer Leasing Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1667, applies to consumers’ leasing of personal property for personal, family, or household use.
text_raw:
CONSUMER LEASING ACT 
The Consumer Leasing Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1667, applies to consumers’ leasing of personal 
property for personal, family, or household use.

text: The Consumer Leasing Act does not apply to leases of personal property that are for business purposes.
text_raw:
The Consumer Leasing Act does not apply to 
leases of personal property that are for business purposes.

text: In order for the Act to apply, the lease must be for longer than four months, and the amount of the lease must be less than $25,000.
text_raw:
In order for the Act to apply, the 
lease must be for longer than four months, and the amount of the lease must be less than 
$25,000.

text: If the Act applies, the consumer must be told the number, the amounts, and the pe- riod of lease payments.
text_raw:
If the Act applies, the consumer must be told the number, the amounts, and the pe- 
riod of lease payments.

text: He or she must also be told the total amount of the payments and be informed about any express warranties offered by either the leasing party or the manufacturer of the property.
text_raw:
He or she must also be told the total amount of the payments and be 
informed about any express warranties offered by either the leasing party or the manufacturer 
of the property.

text: The consumer is also to be told the identity of the person responsible for main- taining or servicing the property, whether he or she has an option to buy the property and the terms of that option, and what happens if he or she ends the lease before the lease expires.
text_raw:
The consumer is also to be told the identity of the person responsible for main- 
taining or servicing the property, whether he or she has an option to buy the property and the 
terms of that option, and what happens if he or she ends the lease before the lease expires.

text: FAIR CREDIT BILLING ACT The Fair Credit Billing Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1666, is a federal law designed to facilitate the settlement of billing errors and to make credit card companies more responsible for the bill that contains the disputed charge.
text_raw:
FAIR CREDIT BILLING ACT 
The Fair Credit Billing Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1666, is a federal law designed to facilitate the 
settlement of billing errors and to make credit card companies more responsible for the bill 
that contains the disputed charge.

text: The creditor must acknowledge the complaint within 30 days and has 90 days to resolve the dispute.
text_raw:
The creditor must acknowledge the complaint within 
30 days and has 90 days to resolve the dispute.

text: The Act also prohibits the mailing of unso- licited credit cards and establishes a process to report lost or stolen cards.
text_raw:
The Act also prohibits the mailing of unso- 
licited credit cards and establishes a process to report lost or stolen cards.

text: CONCLUSION Consumer protection and products liability are two growing areas of law designed to pro- tect consumers from the practices of some manufacturers and retailers.
text_raw:
CONCLUSION 
Consumer protection and products liability are two growing areas of law designed to pro- 
tect consumers from the practices of some manufacturers and retailers.

text: They are based on two broad areas of common law: torts and contracts.
text_raw:
They are based on 
two broad areas of common law: torts and contracts.

text: Product liability was originally based on contract law:
text_raw:
Product liability was originally based 
on contract law:

text: The consumer had to show privity of contract in order to be successful when suing for injury caused by a defective product.
text_raw:
The consumer had to show privity of contract in order to be successful 
when suing for injury caused by a defective product.

text: The contract theory was eventually re- jected by the courts and replaced with the tort theory of the duty to use reasonable care in the manufacture of products.
text_raw:
The contract theory was eventually re- 
jected by the courts and replaced with the tort theory of the duty to use reasonable care in 
the manufacture of products.

text: If reasonable care was not used, then the manufacturer could be held liable for the harm caused.
text_raw:
If reasonable care was not used, then the manufacturer could 
be held liable for the harm caused.

text_raw:
450 CHAPTER 24 
The tort principle of strict liability also began to be applied to products liability.

text: The in- jured consumer no longer has to show a lack of reasonable care to prove liability.
text_raw:
The in- 
jured consumer no longer has to show a lack of reasonable care to prove liability.

text: All the consumer has to prove is that a product is defective, the defect creates an unreasonable risk of harm, and the defect is the proximate cause of the harm.

All the 
consumer has to prove is that a product is defective, the defect creates an unreasonable risk 
of harm, and the defect is the proximate cause of the harm.

text: Strict liability has been applied in cases involving failure to warn, design defect, and unknown hazard.
text_raw:
Strict liability has been applied 
in cases involving failure to warn, design defect, and unknown hazard.

text: Product misuse, as- sumption of the risk, unavoidable danger, learned intermediary, and sophisticated purchaser are defenses to a claim of strict liability.
text_raw:
Product misuse, as- 
sumption of the risk, unavoidable danger, learned intermediary, and sophisticated purchaser 
are defenses to a claim of strict liability.

text: Contract law is still a part of product liability law through the use of warranties, which are statements about the quality or fitness of a product.

Contract law is still a part of product liability law through the use of warranties, which 
are statements about the quality or fitness of a product.

text: A warranty can be written or oral, express or implied, or full or limited, depending on the circumstances and the agreement.

A warranty can be written or oral, 
express or implied, or full or limited, depending on the circumstances and the agreement.

text: Consumer protection occurs primarily by federal law and regulations implemented and regulated by the Federal Trade Commission and the Food and Drug Administration.
text_raw:
Consumer protection occurs primarily by federal law and regulations implemented and 
regulated by the Federal Trade Commission and the Food and Drug Administration.

text: The FDA regulates food products to make sure food has not been adulterated and made unsafe.
text_raw:
The 
FDA regulates food products to make sure food has not been adulterated and made unsafe.

text: The FDA also requires proper labeling so consumers will be informed about what they are eating or taking as medication.
text_raw:
The FDA also requires proper labeling so consumers will be informed about what they are 
eating or taking as medication.

text: The FTC also regulates unfair trade practices and issues industry-wide regulations such as the mail order rule and the used car rule.
text_raw:
The FTC also regulates unfair trade practices and issues industry-wide regulations such 
as the mail order rule and the used car rule.

text: Federal legislation also protects consumer’s rights with regard to credit and debt collection practices, leases, electronic transactions, and billing.
text_raw:
Federal legislation also protects consumer’s 
rights with regard to credit and debt collection practices, leases, electronic transactions, and 
billing.

economy, this is an area of law that will continue to develop and evolve.

text: INTRODUCTION Despite numerous federal and state laws prohibiting it, discrimination still occurs in the workplace, in employment decisions, in the provision of employment benefits, in work as- signments, in wages, and in all other aspects of employment.
text_raw:
INTRODUCTION 
Despite numerous federal and state laws prohibiting it, discrimination still occurs in the 
workplace, in employment decisions, in the provision of employment benefits, in work as- 
signments, in wages, and in all other aspects of employment.

text: Claims of employment dis- crimination are investigated by the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), a federal agency.
text_raw:
Claims of employment dis- 
crimination are investigated by the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), 
a federal agency.

text: The EEOC looks for evidence of either disparate treatment or disparate impact as it analyzes claims of discrimination based on national origin, age, race, religion, disability, or sex.
text_raw:
The EEOC looks for evidence of either disparate treatment or disparate 
impact as it analyzes claims of discrimination based on national origin, age, race, religion, 
disability, or sex.

text: This chapter introduces and discusses terms related to employment discrimination.
text_raw: This chapter introduces and discusses terms related to employment discrimination.

text: It de- scribes the remedies available to those who are victims of workplace discrimination, and explains the defenses commonly invoked in responding to claims of discrimination.
text_raw:
It de- 
scribes the remedies available to those who are victims of workplace discrimination, and 
explains the defenses commonly invoked in responding to claims of discrimination.

text: The ex- hibits in this chapter feature important data that both employers and employees should find interesting.
text_raw:
The ex- 
hibits in this chapter feature important data that both employers and employees should find 
interesting.

text: The chapter concludes with a discussion of government action that is discriminatory and an examination of general defenses to charges of workplace discrimination.
text_raw:
The chapter concludes with a discussion of government action that is discriminatory and 
an examination of general defenses to charges of workplace discrimination.

text: GENERAL PRINCIPLES Discrimination is the unfair treatment of or denial of normal privileges to people because of some inherent characteristic, such as race, age, sex, nationality, or religion.
text_raw:
GENERAL PRINCIPLES 
Discrimination is the unfair treatment of or denial of normal privileges to people because 
of some inherent characteristic, such as race, age, sex, nationality, or religion.

text: Discrimina- tion is the failure to treat all persons equally where no reasonable distinction can be found.
text_raw:
Discrimina- 
tion is the failure to treat all persons equally where no reasonable distinction can be found.

text: Persons of racial or ethnic minorities—African Americans, Hispanics, Asians, Pacific Is- landers, American Indians, or Alaskan Natives—are protected from discrimination.
text_raw:
Persons of racial or ethnic minorities—African Americans, Hispanics, Asians, Pacific Is- 
landers, American Indians, or Alaskan Natives—are protected from discrimination.

text: People are also protected if they are covered by one of the antidiscrimination statutes, for exam- ple, people who are over forty or who have a disability.
text_raw:
People 
are also protected if they are covered by one of the antidiscrimination statutes, for exam- 
ple, people who are over forty or who have a disability.

text: THE EEOC The federal agency responsible for investigating charges of discrimination is the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission or EEOC.
text_raw:
THE EEOC 
The federal agency responsible for investigating charges of discrimination is the Equal 
Employment Opportunity Commission or EEOC.

text: The EEOC is responsible for enforc- ing laws that prohibit discrimination in employment.
text_raw:
The EEOC is responsible for enforc- 
ing laws that prohibit discrimination in employment.

text: The federal government and private individuals can sue in federal court for acts of discrimination not related to employment.
text_raw:
The federal government and private 
individuals can sue in federal court for acts of discrimination not related to employment.

text: DISPARATE IMPACT AND TREATMENT Two types of discrimination are recognized by the EEOC: disparate treatment and dis- parate impact.
text_raw:
DISPARATE IMPACT AND TREATMENT 
Two types of discrimination are recognized by the EEOC: disparate treatment and dis- 
parate impact.

text: Disparate treatment is the act of treating people differently because of their race, sex, religion, color, national origin, or disability.
text_raw:
Disparate treatment is the act of treating people differently because of 
their race, sex, religion, color, national origin, or disability.

text: Disparate treatment is in- tentional discrimination proven either through direct evidence, comparative evidence, or statistical evidence.
text_raw:
Disparate treatment is in-

text: 462 CHAPTER 25 QUID PRO QUO AND HOSTILE WORK ENVIRONMENT There are two forms of workplace sexual harassment: quid pro quo and hostile work envi- ronment.
text_raw:
462 CHAPTER 25 
QUID PRO QUO AND HOSTILE WORK ENVIRONMENT 
There are two forms of workplace sexual harassment: quid pro quo and hostile work envi- 
ronment.

text: In quid pro quo sexual harassment (something for something), sexual favors are sought in return for job benefits or opportunities: “Have sex with me if you want that raise.” “Have sex with me or you are fired.” “Your position with this company would be improved if you would loosen up.” Only a supervisor or manager can commit quid pro quo sexual ha- rassment because only a person with supervisory authority can carry out the threat:
text_raw:
In quid pro quo sexual harassment (something for something), sexual favors are 
sought in return for job benefits or opportunities: “Have sex with me if you want that raise.” 
“Have sex with me or you are fired.” “Your position with this company would be improved 
if you would loosen up.” Only a supervisor or manager can commit quid pro quo sexual ha- 
rassment because only a person with supervisory authority can carry out the threat:

text: Only a supervisor or manager has the power to condition job benefits or opportunities on submis- sion to sexual conduct.
text_raw:
Only a 
supervisor or manager has the power to condition job benefits or opportunities on submis- 
sion to sexual conduct.

text: The demand for sexual favors in return for job benefits can be explicit or implied.
text_raw: The demand for sexual favors in return for job benefits can be explicit or implied.

text: The benefit must be a tangible job benefit, such as the job itself, promotion, leave, pay raises, preferential assignments, and job evaluations.
text_raw:
The 
benefit must be a tangible job benefit, such as the job itself, promotion, leave, pay raises, 
preferential assignments, and job evaluations.

text: One instance of quid pro quo sexual harass- ment is sufficient to constitute a violation of Title VII.
text_raw:
One instance of quid pro quo sexual harass- 
ment is sufficient to constitute a violation of Title VII.

text: The second form of workplace sexual harassment is the hostile work environment.
text_raw: The second form of workplace sexual harassment is the hostile work environment.

text: This term refers to sexual comment or conduct that has the purpose or effect of unrea- sonably interfering with a person’s work performance or creating an intimidating, hostile, or offensive working environment.
text_raw:
This term refers to sexual comment or conduct that has the purpose or effect of unrea- 
sonably interfering with a person’s work performance or creating an intimidating, hostile, 
or offensive working environment.

text: A supervisor or co-worker can be responsible for cre- ating a hostile work environment; this type of harassment does not have to affect a tan- gible job benefit.

A supervisor or co-worker can be responsible for cre- 
ating a hostile work environment; this type of harassment does not have to affect a tan- 
gible job benefit.

text: Rather, it affects the intangible work environment—the work situation itself.

Rather, it affects the intangible work environment—the work situation 
itself.

text: The key issues are frequency and severity:

The more frequent the objectionable 
conduct, the less severe it has to be; the less frequent, the more severe the objectionable 
conduct has to be.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS OF THE JOB AND REASONABLE 
ACCOMMODATIONS 
The ADA requires an employer to identify in writing the essential functions of each job.

text: These “essential functions” are the reason why the job exists.
text_raw: These “essential functions” are the reason why the job exists.

text: A person with a disability must be able to perform those functions either with or without reasonable accommodation.
text_raw:
A person with a disability 
must be able to perform those functions either with or without reasonable accommodation.

text: If the person cannot perform the essential functions of the job, then he or she is not cov- ered by Title I:
text_raw:
If the person cannot perform the essential functions of the job, then he or she is not cov- 
ered by Title I:

text: An employer is required to make reasonable accommodations to allow a person with a disability to perform the essential functions of a job.
text_raw:
An employer is required to make reasonable accommodations to allow a person with a 
disability to perform the essential functions of a job.

text: Reasonable accommodations include assigning the nonessential functions to someone else (this does not mean hiring someone else to do the disabled person’s job), restructuring how the work is done, providing flexi- ble working hours, altering the work site, or providing special equipment.
text_raw:
Reasonable accommodations include 
assigning the nonessential functions to someone else (this does not mean hiring someone 
else to do the disabled person’s job), restructuring how the work is done, providing flexi- 
ble working hours, altering the work site, or providing special equipment.

text: Personal items like eyeglasses and hearing aids do not have to be provided by the employer.
text_raw:
Personal items 
like eyeglasses and hearing aids do not have to be provided by the employer.

text: Reasonable accommodations can also include transfer to a vacant position, provided the position is, in fact, vacant and the person is qualified for the position.

accommodations can also include transfer to a vacant position, provided the position is, in

text: The accommodation provided does not have to be the one requested, as long as it is ef- fective.

The accommodation provided does not have to be the one requested, as long as it is ef- 
fective.

text: The person with a disability is held to the same standards as everyone else.

Prior to 1972, the federal government had little if any control over pollution expelled into 
the nation’s waters.

text: The Clean Water Act, passed in 1972, gave the federal government control over water pollution.
text_raw:
The Clean Water Act, passed in 1972, gave the federal government 
control over water pollution.

text: The goal of the Clean Water Act is to protect the integrity of the national water system.

The goal of the Clean Water Act is to protect the integrity of 
the national water system.

text: There are five major components to the Clean Water Act.
text_raw: There are five major components to the Clean Water Act.

text: It allows the EPA to establish national effluent (pollution) standards, which set water pollution limits for every industry that discharges liquid wastes into na- tional waterways.

It allows the EPA to establish national effluent (pollution) standards, which set 
water pollution limits for every industry that discharges liquid wastes into na- 
tional waterways.

period of time.

text: POINT AND NONPOINT SOURCE POLLUTION Water pollution is identified as either point source pollution or nonpoint source pollution.
text_raw:
POINT AND NONPOINT SOURCE POLLUTION 
Water pollution is identified as either point source pollution or nonpoint source pollution.

text: Point source pollution is emitted from a definitive place of discharge, such as a pipe, ditch, or channel.
text_raw:
Point source pollution is emitted from a definitive place of discharge, such as a pipe, ditch, 
or channel.

text: The location where point source pollution originates is easy to identify and usu- ally easy to treat.

The location where point source pollution originates is easy to identify and usu- 
ally easy to treat.

text: Nonpoint source pollution is created by several sources, making it im- _ possible to specifically identify where it originated.

Nonpoint source pollution is created by several sources, making it im- _ 
possible to specifically identify where it originated.

text: Nonpoint source pollution includes runoff from streets, agricultural runoff, and pollution from construction, logging opera- tions, and mining sites.
text_raw:
Nonpoint source pollution includes 
runoff from streets, agricultural runoff, and pollution from construction, logging opera- 
tions, and mining sites.

text: There are regulations in place that attempt to control this type of pollution, but because the exact source cannot be identified, nonpoint source pollution is more difficult to regulate and control.
text_raw:
There are regulations in place that attempt to control this type of 
pollution, but because the exact source cannot be identified, nonpoint source pollution is 
more difficult to regulate and control.

text: The treatment of sewage from point source pollution usually takes place at a publicly owned treatment works (POTWs), a publicly owned facility that removes pollutants from the water.

The treatment of sewage from point source pollution usually takes place at a publicly 
owned treatment works (POTWs), a publicly owned facility that removes pollutants from 
the water.

text: Because most of the pollutants treated at POTWs are nontoxic, the sludge— material that is removed from the water during treatment—is often used for fertilizer.

text: DRINKING WATER In addition to passing laws regulating the discharge of pollution into water, the federal gov- ernment has also created laws designed specifically to protect our country’s drinking water supply.
text_raw:
DRINKING WATER 
In addition to passing laws regulating the discharge of pollution into water, the federal gov- 
ernment has also created laws designed specifically to protect our country’s drinking water 
supply.

text: The Safe Drinking Water Act sets standards for the drinking water supplied by public water supply systems.
text_raw:
The Safe Drinking Water Act sets standards for the drinking water supplied by 
public water supply systems.

text: A public water supply system is any system that has at least fifteen service connections or that serves twenty-five or more people.
text_raw:
A public water supply system is any system that has at least 
fifteen service connections or that serves twenty-five or more people.

text: Under this Act, the EPA is required to establish two levels of drinking water standards: primary standards and secondary standards.
text_raw:

primary standards and secondary standards.

text: Primary standards protect human health and secondary standards protect the aesthetic quality of drinking water.
text_raw:
Primary standards protect human health and 
secondary standards protect the aesthetic quality of drinking water.

text: Primary standards are based on maximum contaminant level goals—levels where there are no potential adverse health effects.
text_raw:
Primary standards are 
based on maximum contaminant level goals—levels where there are no potential adverse 
health effects.

text_raw:
Maximum containment level goals are not enforceable standards, but rather

man health effects.

text: Maximum contaminant levels are enforceable by the EPA.

text: The CDA differs from the various laws and orders upheld in those cases in many ways, including that __ it does not allow parents fo consent to their children’s use of restricted materials; is not limited to commercial transactions; fails to provide any definition of “indecent” and omits any requirement that “patently offensive” material lack socially redeeming value; neither limits its broad categorical prohibitions to particular times nor bases them on an evaluation by an agency familiar with the medium’s unique characteristics; is punitive; applies - toa medium that, unlike radio, receives full First Amendment protection; and cannot be properly analyzed as a form of time, place, and manner regulation because it is a content-based blanket restriction on speech.

The CDA differs from the various laws and orders upheld in those cases in many ways, including that 
__ it does not allow parents fo consent to their children’s use of restricted materials; is not limited to commercial
